newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Dec 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following the High Court's controversial decision on the Wik case yesterday, which found that pastoral leases did not always extinguish native title, some State Governments, farmers and miners have warned that the ruling will stall development on the 40 percent of Australia covered by pastoral leases and scare off potential investors because of uncertainty and legal costs. Page 1.

The Federal Government introduced new regulations earlier this month that exclude new groups of employees from Federal unfair dismissal protection, such as casual workers, probationers, employees on fixed-term contracts and workers away from work because f illness. Page 3.

The latest Morgan poll, taken in the middle of this month, shows support for the Federal Coalition Government was unchanged at 48 per cent, and the Labor Opposition's support increased by 1.5 per cent to 36.5 per cent. Both the Australian Democrats and te Greens lost support. Page 2.

Following talks between the Australian and Japanese Governments last week, Qantas Airways, Ansett Australia and All Nippon Airways have revealed plans to increase flights between Australia and Japan. Transport Minister John Sharp said the Government talk will allow the equivalent of another four Boeing 767s, or two Boeing 747s, in two stages from March 30 and October 26. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a rejection of a key plank of the Federal Government's native title policy, the High Court ruled yesterday that native title can survive on pastoral leases. The decision immediately prompted calls from the Queensland and West Australian Governments for Federal protection of landholders who previously thought their land was secure from claim, but Prime Minister John Howard last night refused to say whether the Government would amend the Native Title Act. Page 1.

The sole representative for the Wik people in the High Court yesterday, Gladys Tybingoompa celebrated the victory with a traditional celebratory dance outside the court. Tybingoompa said the decision was like a gateway to allow her people to say what the feel about their land, ceremonies, ways and culture, but the Wik still have to battle their claim in the Federal Court. Page 1.

The Hobart Supreme Court yesterday ordered that the assets of Port Arthur killer Martin Bryant be forfeited to the State and distributed to the victims, their families and the survivors of the April 28 massacre. The director of public prosecutions , Damian Bugg QC, estimated that Bryant's victims would receive about A$1 million after Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Finance Minister John Fahey agreed to waive the personal income tax Bryant would normally be liable to pay. Page 3.

Two Aboriginal boys accused of spitting on Independent MP Pauline Hanson will be allowed to spend Christmas with their families, after a Children's Court judge yesterday overturned a decision that they remain in custody for six weeks pending a trial. The boys, aged 11 and 12, will be sent to a rural training farm. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In the most significant judgement since the Mabo decision on the existence of native title in 1992, the High Court yesterday ruled that native title and pastoral leases could co-exist and that the granting of a pastoral lease did not necessarily extinguis native title. National Farmers Federation president Donald McGauchie said the decision would create "interminable legal wrangles", but Aboriginal leaders said they would use the decision to pressure the Government to drop planned amendments to the Native Title Act. Page 1.

Despite growing concerns that the national economy is faltering, Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday indicated that New South Wales is surging ahead with a boom-time rate of economic growth at around five per cent. September quarter gross State product data revealed that New South Wales experienced the fastest rate of growth in any State, up 1.6 per cent in trend terms and current prices. Page 1.

Sydney Swans full forward Tony Lockett has been charged with deception and false documentation in relation to alleged breeding irregularities involving his champion stud dog, Malawi's Prince. Lockett will appear in the Melbourne Magistrates Court on Febrary 19 in conjunction with Darren McDonald, a trainer and breeder who was charged with 28 counts of deception last week. Page 1.

Drummoyne man Brian Hall will now face a charge of murder after one of his alleged victims in a drunken row died on the weekend. After being run down by a car, 18-year-old Brooke Webber suffered massive head injuries and was in a coma before dying peaceflly on Sunday morning. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a 4-3 majority decision yesterday, the High Court accepted an appeal by the Wik and Thayorre people of Cape York against a Federal Court decision that had found that pastoral leases extinguished native title. The decision means native title disputes wll have to be settled case by case, prompting pastoralists and miners to call on the Federal Government to legislate to end uncertainty and an explosion of legal cases. Page A1.

After being re-installed as the Victorian Opposition Leader yesterday, John Brumby said the results of the caucus meeting were a "ringing endorsement" of his program of change. Health spokesman John Thwaites defeated the Socialist Left's Demetri Dollis for the deputy leadership and Labor's ethnic affairs spokesman Biddie Micallef was dumped in favour of Don Nardella. Page A1.

Saudi Arabian officials have detained two British nurses for questioning in a Dhahran prison in connection with the murder of Australian nurse, Yvonne Gilford. British embassy staff have been refused access to the two Britons, who if charged and found gulty, will automatically face the death penalty. Page A1.

Australian Football League star Tony Lockett was yesterday charged with nine counts of deception and 18 counts of false documentation after police questioned him over alleged breeding irregularities involving his champion stud greyhound, Malawi's Prince. Lockett has been granted bail and will appear at the Melbourne Magistrates Court on February 19. Page A1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
